status: Step 1 source coverage for the free scalar wedge modular-geometry pair. Full source PDFs were inspected at the listed sections; source-fetch-check stamps are added after retrieval.

sources.title: Joseph J. Bisognano and Eyvind H. Wichmann, On the duality condition for a Hermitian scalar field, Journal of Mathematical Physics 16 (1975), 985–1007
sources.locator: Complete 24-page PDF inspected at §II (PDF pp. 2–5), §IV and Theorem 1 (pp. 7–10), and §V (pp. 10–15). The source states the field assumptions, analytic continuation of wedge boosts, cyclic/separating conditions, and the relation to Tomita theory; this carrier adopts the geometric bridge explicitly rather than transferring its field hypotheses without proof.

contents.name: §II: Poincare representation, forward spectrum, vacuum and scalar-field assumptions
contents.support: Records the source's global hypotheses. The local postulate states its own scalar Fock model and explicitly adopts wedge standardness.

contents.name: §IV, Theorem 1: complex boost analyticity and wedge relation
contents.support: Primary source for the geometric modular/boost bridge. The identity remains an adopted model interface here; this citation is not substituted for a local proof.

contents.name: §V: relation of the wedge construction to Tomita theory
contents.support: Supports the distinction between abstract modular data and their additional geometric identification.

contents.name: §VI–VII: further wedge duality conditions and bounded-region duality
contents.reason: The assigned pair adopts no Haag-duality theorem, bounded-region construction, or additional local extension condition.

sources.title: Daniele Guido, Modular theory for the von Neumann algebras of local quantum physics, complete lecture notes, arXiv:0812.1511
sources.locator: Complete 28-page PDF inspected at §2.1 (PDF pp. 2–10), §§3.1.1–3.1.2 (pp. 14–17), and §3.3 (p. 20). The free scalar one-particle representation, wedge modular relation, standardness discussion, and KMS interpretation were read. Its (+---) metric and boost parameter are translated to the local (-+++) future-boost convention.

contents.name: §2.1: massive free scalar one-particle space, Poincare action, local real subspaces and Fock lift
contents.support: Independent full lecture-notes treatment of the selected free scalar and its local observable construction.

contents.name: §3.1.1: one-particle Bisognano–Wichmann relation for the right wedge
contents.support: States the geometric modular action for the free scalar; source rapidity sign is converted explicitly in the local boost convention.

contents.name: §3.1.2 and §3.3: Wightman wedge standardness and KMS/acceleration interpretation
contents.support: Provides an independent treatment of the wedge-KMS interpretation. The local proof uses its explicit suppliers, not this source as a proof.

contents.name: Conformal-net and non-wedge modular-covariance results
contents.reason: The item is confined to one massive free scalar right wedge and does not claim general conformal or arbitrary-region results.

sources.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1803.04993
sources.locator: Complete 80-page PDF inspected at §§5.2–5.4 (PDF pp. 47–56), especially §5.3 (pp. 53–54) and §5.4 (pp. 54–56). The path-integral discussion explicitly notes its lack of rigor at the wedge boundary; the later section sketches the Bisognano–Wichmann holomorphy argument and the accelerated-clock strip.

contents.name: §5.3: holomorphy sketch of the Bisognano–Wichmann wedge relation
contents.support: Independent sign and strip-width context; Witten labels it a brief sketch, so it supplies no step of the authored proof.

contents.name: §5.4: hyperbolic accelerated orbit and KMS strip of width 2 pi R
contents.support: Supports the proper-time/boost clock comparison. The SI conversion and W*-algebra proof are derived locally.

contents.name: §5.2: Euclidean path-integral factorization argument
contents.reason: The author explicitly says the factorization/path-integral argument is not altogether rigorous; no continuum tensor factorization is adopted here.

sources.title: Stefan Hollands and Robert M. Wald, Quantum fields in curved spacetime, arXiv:1401.2026
sources.locator: Complete 77-page review inspected at §2.2(a), PDF pp. 20–22, and the general KMS discussion in §2.1, PDF pp. 17–19. The Rindler wedge, boost time, restricted-vacuum KMS statement, natural-unit convention, and distinction from detector interpretation were read.

contents.name: §2.2(a): Rindler wedge and restricted Minkowski-vacuum KMS theorem
contents.support: Independent source for the algebraic Rindler KMS context and its boost normalization; the source's massless two-point calculation is not used as a premise.

contents.name: §2.2(a): detector interpretation
contents.support: Read to preserve the distinction between the KMS state and a detector model; no response probability or observation is claimed.

contents.name: Curved-spacetime Hadamard and black-hole applications
contents.reason: The assigned model is flat Minkowski space and asserts no Hawking or curved-background result.

sources.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, arXiv:gr-qc/9912119
sources.locator: Complete 46-page review inspected at §3, printed pp. 11–16 (PDF pp. 12–16). The boost-invariant Minkowski vacuum, Unruh KMS interpretation, normalization of the boost clock, and distinction between Unruh and Hawking states were read; the source sets c, hbar and k_B to one.

contents.name: §3: Unruh effect as a wedge KMS state and distinction from Hawking radiation
contents.support: Supports the model-scope warning that the Minkowski-vacuum Unruh effect and black-hole Hawking state are distinct. Its natural-unit formula is not used for the SI derivation.

contents.name: Black-hole collapse, Hawking flux and generalized second law
contents.reason: No horizon formation, radiation flux, or generalized entropy claim is made in this pair.

sources.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras, arXiv:2004.02383
sources.locator: Complete 159-page lecture notes inspected at §2.2, Definition 2.11 and Theorem 2.14 (PDF pp. 17–19). Hiai writes the KMS condition on a lower strip and the modular case at beta = -1; the local carrier follows its exact upper-strip supplier instead.

contents.name: §2.2, Definition 2.11: KMS strip boundary convention
contents.support: Read as a convention comparison only. The local proof is an explicit reparameterization of the upper-strip W*-KMS supplier and does not inherit Hiai's lower-strip sign.

contents.name: §2.2, Theorem 2.14: Takesaki KMS condition
contents.support: Confirms that the modular KMS assertion is an operator-algebra boundary condition; no theorem from Hiai is used in the local rescaling proof.

sources.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1311.2717
sources.locator: Complete 157-page lecture notes inspected at §3.4, Definition 3.4.4 (printed pp. 74–75, PDF pp. 73–74). It states the C*-dynamical upper-strip boundary condition with physical width hbar beta and a strongly continuous automorphism group.

contents.name: §3.4, Definition 3.4.4: C*-dynamical physical-time KMS strip
contents.support: Used to check the unit convention and identify the norm-continuity mismatch. The local lemma proves the needed W*-strip scaling directly.

sources.title: Daniel Harlow, Jerusalem Lectures on Black Holes and Quantum Information, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1409.1231
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted lecture notes inspected at §§3.2–3.3 (the entanglement analogy and Rindler decomposition, PDF pages around 18–22). The local example's oscillator normalization, partial trace and entropy are independently derived; Harlow's continuum discussion is context, not a factorization proof.

contents.name: §3.2: finite-system entanglement analogy for quantum-field correlations
contents.support: Motivates the finite-mode illustration; the exact infinite oscillator series in the item is proved locally.

contents.name: §3.3: Rindler decomposition and continuum-factorization caveat
contents.support: Supports the distinction between a two-factor oscillator example and a continuum local-algebra construction; no tensor-factorization theorem is imported.

contents.name: Black-hole holography and later applications
contents.reason: The example makes no holographic, black-hole entropy, or empirical claim.

sources.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1803.04993
sources.locator: Complete 80-page lecture notes inspected at §§5.2–5.3 (PDF pp. 47–54). Section 5.2 explicitly qualifies the Euclidean path-integral/factorization account as nonrigorous; the local example uses this as a scope warning, not as proof of oscillator identities.

contents.name: §5.2: Euclidean path-integral/factorization discussion and its rigor qualification
contents.support: The source explicitly flags the continuum factorization account as nonrigorous; the item therefore limits its calculation to the two declared oscillator factors.

contents.name: §5.3: Bisognano–Wichmann holomorphy discussion
contents.reason: The B example proves finite oscillator identities and makes no modular-covariance or wedge-KMS claim.
